findings.reason: the mechanism's warning would name the plan total for a long plan's short section, and the done-when fixture ("a plan whose section declares six hours of effort") sets up a figure `_estimated_hours` never reads, so an implementer following the sentence and one following the test build different readers and one of them fails its own gate.
findings.text: the deliverable says "The estimate is the one `_estimated_hours` in `reckon/crew/routing.py` already resolves: the node's own estimate, else its plan section's effort", but `_estimated_hours` (routing.py:3465) falls back to `_plan_html.parse_meta(...).get("effort_hours")`, which is the plan's authored `plan-effort-hours` meta — the same figure for every section of a plan (measured at head: sections s52 and s46 of this plan both resolve to `(17.5, 'plan-fallback')`) — and not the section's `data-effort-hours`

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `reckon/schema/flight-defaults.yaml`, `reckon/crew/routing.py`, `_estimated_hours` (routing.py:3465), `_effective_backend` (routing.py:146) and `reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py` all resolve; the 8m implement default is confirmed by `git blame` at `d5d3c3513` (2026-08-17); and both cited run ids (`r-20261021T114725739639`, `r-20261021T142211695258`) exist under the crew state tree.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §52's done-when names a base arm, five falsifiable cases, and an explicit negative control ("Remove the warning, and the six-hour case must fail"), so the guard can be shown to fire rather than resting on a suite that passes on the unfixed code.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the done-when places both arms' logs and the ruff log "in the run directory", a durable path a later reader can open, never a session scratchpad or node-local temporary.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new file name `test_a_bare_dispatch_names_a_fence_far_below_its_effort.py` states the mechanism and carries no plan label, ticket number or version tag.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §52 describes `_estimated_hours`'s fallback as "its plan section's effort", but that function returns the plan's authored `plan-effort-hours` total, identical for every section, which contradicts the done-when's six-hour *section* fixture.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §52 carries one deliverable (a dispatch warning when a default fence sits far below the node's estimate); the CLI-stderr measurement is that same deliverable read through a second reader, not a second goal.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §52 declares no `depends-on` and needs none: it reads existing symbols (`_estimated_hours`, `resolved_time_budget`) and writes `reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py` plus one new test, and no other section declares an edge to it (correctly, `plan-section-depends-on` carries no `s52` entry).
